title: Reading Hieroglyphs and Tomb Warnings
heading: Legible Scripts
summary: Explains the medieval belief that learned Copts can read hieroglyphs, and gives a stress roll with Ease Factors for grasping the gist of tomb warnings and curses as taught by the Seekers' Guild.
quotes: the gist of a text can be understood with an Intelligence + Profession: Seeker stress roll against an Ease Factor related to the age and complexity of the text (common curses are Ease Factor 6, typical texts are Ease Factor 9)

title: Hazards of the Desert
heading: Hazards of the Desert
summary: Adjusts the Deprivation rules for desert travel (faster water checks, extra sun damage) and gives a stress roll to escape dry quicksand, with notes on brigands, storms and jinn.
quotes: The Deprivation check time for lack of water is reduced in the deserts to 4 hours, while the sunlight does +1 non-combat damage if skin is left exposed
A character who is caught in an area of dry quicksand may make a Strength or Quickness stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9 in the first round

title: Languages of the Nile and Dialect Penalties
heading: Languages
summary: Lists the living languages and dialects of Egypt, Nubia and Ethiopia (dialects as specialties), and gives a table of penalties applied to both speakers when related languages or dialects meet.
quotes: Mahasi is on the verge of separating into a separate language, and those who know this dialect have a larger penalty than usual when talking to speakers of the other Nubian dialects.

title: Dead Languages of the Nile
heading: Dead Languages
summary: Describes the dead languages Ancient Egyptian, Demotic, Meroitic and Ge'ez, how they relate to living tongues, and their scripts.

title: The Dhimmi Flaw in Egypt
heading: Non-Muslim Characters: The Dhimmi Flaw
summary: Explains the legal status of non-Muslims in Egypt and lists what a dhimmi character must not do, which is the extended rule behind the Minor General Flaw Dhimmi; European characters may use Outsider instead.
quotes: Their duties and proscriptions are reflected in the Dhimmi Flaw, which is a Minor General Flaw. Characters from Europe might use Outsider instead.

title: The Future and Hex Rolls
heading: The Future
summary: Boasting about future plans without saying 'if God wills it' is believed to invite curses, giving envious characters a bonus on Hex rolls unless the protective phrase is used.
quotes: This is represented as a +6 bonus on Hex rolls, to destroy the circumstance discussed, by any character who envies the speaker.

title: Reputations, Shame and the Haj
heading: Reputations and Shame
summary: Describes how characters remove a shameful Local Reputation by building a rival Reputation and buying down the old one, and how the Haj pilgrimage is treated as a series of scenes granting Reputation experience.
quotes: Once the competing Reputation equals the undesired Reputation, new experience gained in the second Reputation can instead be used to buy down the first
The Haj is, from a game perspective, a series of scenes.

title: Pretending to Be Male or Married (Dark Secrets)
heading: Dark Secrets?
summary: Advice on when a female character's disguise as a man or as a married woman counts as a Dark Secret or Gender Nonconforming Flaw, and when it is only a convenience.
quotes: If it will ruin the character's life, it is a Dark Secret.

title: Overrun (creature Quality)
heading: Hippopotamus
requires: Creature with the Overrun Quality (hippopotamus, elephant)
summary: A charging creature that hits with Overrun knocks its opponent down on a failed Dexterity + Athletics stress roll, after which the opponent is prone and cannot parry. The rule appears in the hippopotamus stat block and is reused for the elephant.
quotes: the opponent must make a Dexterity + Athletics stress roll against an Ease Factor equal to (Damage Total (before soak) + hippopotamus's Size – opponent's Size)

title: Roll Attack and Drowning (crocodile)
heading: Crocodile (Cocodryllus)
requires: Creature with the Roll Attack Quality (crocodile)
summary: A crocodile that has bitten a foe can roll next round to tear flesh or drag the victim underwater to drown, and a victim breaks free only by overcoming a Grapple. The block also gives stealth, ambush and Crushing Jaws notes.
quotes: doing +6 damage without an attack roll
This requires the character to overcome a successful Grapple attack with a Grapple Strength of 10.

title: Crushing Jaws (creature Quality)
heading: New Quality
requires: Creature with the Crushing Jaws Quality (hyena, crocodile)
summary: A new animal Quality for creatures with tremendously powerful biting muscles; the jaws can be held shut with a successful Grapple.
quotes: This Quality adds +3 Damage to any bite attack.

title: Constriction and Swallow Whole (giant serpents)
heading: Serpent, Elephant-Eating
requires: Creature with the Constriction or Swallow Whole Quality
summary: Rules for a serpent that constricts a grappled victim (deprivation checks) and can swallow smaller prey whole, where stomach acid does damage each round unless the victim braces against immersion. Includes group-attack tactics against elephants.
quotes: The victim must make a Stamina check every five rounds, or suffer the normal effects of deprivation.
The powerful acids inflict +9 damage every round, complete immersion quadruples this to +36

title: The Seekers' Guild and Profession: Seeker
heading: The Seekers' Guild (Al-Matalibeen)
summary: Describes the licensed Egyptian guild of tomb-robbers, its membership cost, library and training benefits, and the Profession: Seeker Ability that represents its lore.
quotes: Membership is purchased with an annual fee and a slice of the recovered treasure. This is currently 20% of all valuables found.
This knowledge is covered by the Profession: Seeker Ability.

title: How Egyptian Tombs Sustain Ghosts
heading: The Structure of Tombs
summary: Explains the Egyptian afterlife in the Magic Realm: a ka must return each year to feed from offerings in its tomb or risk becoming a mut, and each tomb has a chapel, serdab and sepulcher with different defenses.
quotes: A ghost that does not do this risks losing its memories and becoming a mut, or else fading away entirely.

title: Serdab and Stele
heading: Serdab
summary: The serdab is the ghost's home in a tomb; a ghost can manifest any item from its grave goods or tomb paintings, and the stele in the serdab is the doorway to Duat and the Field of Reeds.
quotes: An Egyptian ghost can manifest, as part of its ethereal form, any item found in its grave goods or depicted on its tomb walls, provided they have not been stolen or defaced.

title: Ghosts Animating Statues
heading: Statues
summary: Egyptian ghosts prefer to be incarnate and animate statues that resemble their bodies, which is why servant statues (ushabtis) and defacing statues matter to tomb robbers.
quotes: Defacement prevents a ghost animating a statue from ambushing the thieves, and deanimates those already possessed

title: Tomb Auras, the Stele Vestige and Mummies as Arcane Connections
heading: Tombs, Temples, and Auras
summary: Tombs commonly lie in Magic auras and their stele is a vestige whose level equals the aura; an intact mummy is an Arcane Connection that helps the ka's Vestige Travel Total. Temples tend toward weak Faerie auras.
quotes: The stele within the tomb's serdab is a vestige to the Magic Realm with a level equal to the Magic aura within the tomb.
granting a Familiarity Bonus to the Vestige Travel Total of 15

title: Ghosts Carving Equipment
heading: Carving Equipment
summary: A ghost buried with carving tools can make representations of objects that become real for its purposes, with creation time depending on the age of the tomb, and can feed itself or summon faerie reinforcements.
quotes: so the ghost can create a new object by drawing it in a single round

title: The Field of Reeds
heading: The Field of Reeds
summary: Describes the Egyptian afterlife regio in the Magic Realm, an archipelago of paradise islands ruled by the Daimon Wesir, each with a stele linking to a tomb, and its Faerie copy ruled by Osiris.

title: Resolving Tomb Traps
heading: Mechanical Traps
summary: An optional trap procedure in which each player frames a clever response and rolls only for it against a trap Ease Factor the storyguide adjusts per character, with actions resolved in Quickness order (endangered character first, trap last), Fast-Cast magic and Action Priority Rolls.
quotes: Each trap is assigned a base Ease Factor, indicating the complexity of its construction.
The actions are resolved in order of Quickness, but with the character actually in danger always being treated as fastest, and the trap always going last.

title: Tomb Curses: Condition and Excoriation
heading: Curses
summary: Egyptian tomb curses are written enchantments made of a condition that triggers them and one or more excoriations that deliver the penalty; the storyguide decides how literally the condition is read.
quotes: All curses have two parts: a **condition** and one or more **excoriations**.

title: Egyptian Talismans (tomb magic)
heading: Talismans
summary: Describes trigger-based Egyptian talismans, which lack Penetration against humans, can be temporarily deactivated by a particular spell, and can be investigated like item triggers or resolved as narrative traps with a base Ease Factor from the effect's magnitude.
quotes: The base Ease Factor for bypassing a magical trap is equal to (6 + the magnitude of its effect).

title: Possess Statue (Minor Power)
heading: Possess Statue (Minor Power)
requires: Egyptian ghost with the Possess Statue power
summary: A power letting a ghost animate a wooden, stone or metal statue, given with a Hermetic equivalent level for each material; the statue's physical attacks must penetrate opponents' Magic Resistance.
quotes: Note that the physical attacks of an animated statue have to Penetrate the Magic Resistance of any opponents struck.

title: Egyptian Wards (tomb magic)
heading: Wards
summary: Egyptian wards hide tombs or repel intruders, usually with a defined way to deactivate them, may carry Penetration against spirits, and are overcome with the narrative trap rules at a base Ease Factor from the effect's magnitude.
quotes: The base Ease Factor for such actions is (9 + the magnitude of effect).

title: Quick Ghost Conversion (ka)
heading: Quick Ghost Conversion Notes
summary: A step-by-step kit for turning an ordinary character into an Egyptian ghost (ka): choose Magic Might, swap Virtues and Flaws, add Magic Spirit, note intangibility and vulnerability to Mentem, and add powers and vis.
quotes: Give the character a Magic Might score of between 5 and 25
Add vis, usually Mentem, equal to the Might score divided by 5.

title: Quick Animated Statue Conversion
heading: Quick Animated Statue Conversion Notes
summary: A kit for building an animated statue from a mortal character, including Soak by statue material, size adjustments to Strength and Quickness, damage penalties for stone or bronze weapons, and how to force a ghost out of a statue.
quotes: Wood grants +9 Soak.
Hard metal grants +21 Soak.
Characters lose 2 Strength and gain 1 Quickness per Size lost, or conversely gain 2 Strength and lose 1 Quickness per Size gained.

title: Royal Pharaonic Ghosts
heading: Detailed Design for Royal Pharaonic Ghosts
summary: Guidelines for designing the ghosts of Egyptian royalty: bloodline Virtues from Faerie gods, odd powers drawn from a pharaoh's life, and Transformation after death thanks to long death rituals.
related: Realms of Power: Magic p.52 Transformation

title: Blood of the Old Gods and Sympathy Traits
heading: New Virtue: Blood of the Old Gods
requires: Virtue: Blood of the Old Gods (Minor or Major Supernatural)
summary: A variety of Faerie Blood that grants a Sympathy Trait which can replace an Ability speciality on applicable rolls (always as a stress roll), is raised with experience, and is capped by the Warping Score.
quotes: A Sympathy Trait can replace the character's speciality on any applicable Ability roll, but doing so always makes the roll a stress roll.

title: The Akh (Egyptian Daimon)
heading: The Akh
summary: Explains how the ba, ka and khu fuse into an akh, a Daimon, and how to build one as a Magic Spirit with a Magic Might range, as a Winter creature summoned by name or relics.
quotes: Assume a Magic Might Score of 20 for noblemen who have the simplest coffin texts, up to 60 for the greatest pharaohs

title: Designing Tombs and Mortuaries
heading: Designing Tombs and Mortuaries
summary: Introduces a method for designing ancient tombs with Boons, Hooks and Build Points as if they were covenants, needed only if a tomb is an ongoing part of a saga.
quotes: This section presents a method for designing ancient tombs using Boons, Hooks, and Build Points as if it were a covenant.

title: Basic Tomb Features: Tether, Aura and Build Points
heading: Basic Tomb Features
summary: Tombs generate preternatural tethers that create Magic auras, and the tomb's rank sets its base aura and Build Points; each tomb has a cap on Hook points to spend on Boons.
quotes: For every century that a grave site (which could be a series of pyramids, or a number of individual tombs) was in use, it generates a tether score of 1, up to a maximum of 5.
Each tomb can have up to 10 points of Hooks, which can be used to purchase Boons.

title: Tomb Curses as Resources
heading: Curses
summary: How to build a tomb curse as a Hermetic-style enchantment: usual Range and Target, triggers, uses per day, Greater or Lesser Malediction for effects Hermetic magic cannot copy, false curses and their Build Point cost.
quotes: Maledictions can be of any appropriate Technique or Form, and have a base level of 10 for a Lesser Malediction, and level 30 for a Greater Malediction.
A curse costs two Build Points for every five levels of effects.

title: Tomb Enchanted Items: Talismans and Wards
heading: Enchanted Items (Talismans and Wards)
summary: Sets the Build Point cost of tomb talismans and wards and notes that they are not true Hermetic enchantments, so they can be bypassed using the trap Ease Factors, with Magic Resistance beating low Penetration automatically.
quotes: These cost two Build Points for every five levels of effects.

title: Tomb Specialists
heading: Specialists
summary: Tomb inhabitants such as cult priests, walking cadavers and ghostly viziers are bought as specialists, teachers or guardians for Build Points.
quotes: Tomb guardians usually cost Build Points equal to their highest Martial Ability or Brawl, as applicable.

title: Example Traps and Trap Damage
heading: Example Traps
summary: A catalogue of mechanical traps with Build Costs and Ease Factors, including rules of thumb for rockfall, projectile and pit damage, head wires and poisoned powders.
quotes: For smaller rockfalls, a rule of thumb is +1 damage per 10 pounds of rocks.
calculate Damage as (Stress die + Weapon Damage Modifier from page 177 of the core rules)

title: Tomb Traps: Build Point Costs
heading: Traps
summary: Tables giving the Build Point cost of tomb traps by severity of harm and the modifier for how hard they are to avoid.
quotes: The ease of avoiding a trap modifies the Build Point cost.

title: Tomb Hooks and Boons
heading: Hooks and Boons
summary: Notes how covenant Boons and Hooks apply to tombs: Wealth means intact grave goods, and Nubian tombs should take the Seclusion Boon.
quotes: In Nubia, all tombs should purchase the Seclusion Boon due to the superstitious avoidance of all things to do with the dead.

title: Means of Avoiding Traps
heading: Means of Avoiding Traps
summary: Traps take effect last in the combat round so characters can react, and slower traps such as flooding rooms give extended time to escape.
quotes: Traps, regardless of their type, impose their effects last in the combat round.

title: Perception Checks and Trap Lighting
heading: Perception Checks and Traps
summary: A Perception + Awareness roll lets a character notice a trap without triggering it, with Ease Factors modified by the quality of lighting.
quotes: Characters able to supply perfect lighting conditions (such as through a spell) decrease the Ease Factor by 3

title: Evading Traps with Lords of Men Evasion
heading: Evading Traps
requires: Optional Combat rules from Lords of Men
summary: For troupes using the optional Lords of Men combat rules, a trap's Attack total is based on the trap setter's Intelligence and Profession and tested against the Evasion Combat Statistic.
quotes: assume the trap's Attack total is stress die + Intelligence of the trap setter + Profession of the trap setter

title: Books of the Lector Priests (Faerie Rite Wizards)
heading: Books of The Lector Priests
requires: Tradition: Faerie Rite Wizards (Realms of Power: Faerie)
summary: Lector priests were Faerie Rite Wizards whose books of rites hold closely related effects (Evocation, Grant, Weal, Ware, Woe) performed with the Ceremony Special Ability.
quotes: all priests had the Ceremony Special Ability (page 115)

title: Even Ancient Egyptians Thought Monumental Tombs Were Weird
heading: Even Ancient Egyptians Thought Monumental Tombs Were Weird
summary: Explains that the tomb chapter assumes Magic-aligned practitioners while this chapter describes Faerie-aligned priests served by Magic-aligned artisans, and that artefacts from either system may be used.
quotes: Artefacts designed under either system should be used in a troupe's saga, as suits their stories.

title: Reading the Books of Ritual
heading: Reading the Books of Ritual
summary: How a character performs an Ancient Egyptian rite from a book: a Communication + Coptic roll against a target based on effect level, ritual preparation and purity, a required Faerie aura, and reasons rites fail.
quotes: This may require a Communication + Leadership roll against a target of 3 + 1 per required follower.
the character must make a Communication + Coptic roll of 3 + (1 per 5 levels of effect)

title: Heka and Faerie-Based Egyptian Magic
heading: Heka
summary: Explains heka, the Egyptian name for vis and written spells, and that Egyptian religious magic is mainly Faerie-based, so flourishes such as dawn casting and animal sacrifice were not optional.
quotes: Egyptian religious magic differed from Hermetic magic in that it is primarily based on the Faerie, not Magical, realm.

title: Egyptian Views of Vis
heading: Vis
summary: Describes the materials the Egyptians thought held heka, such as resin, gold, iron and deformed things, which tomb robbers often discard without realizing they are vis.
quotes: Resin, for example, was thought to contain heka that could be used for preservation magic

title: Egyptian Rites Without Realms of Power: Faerie
heading: Troupes Not Using Realms of Power: Faerie
summary: A Hermetic substitute for Faerie Rites: after a Communication + Coptic roll, the reader makes a casting total from Stamina, closest Form and Technique, and Aura, with a table of Fatigue loss and Warping by result; Egyptian books are treated as casting tablets.
quotes: the character must make a Communication + Coptic roll against an Ease Factor of 3 + (1 per 5 levels of effect)
The speaker's casting total is: Stamina + closest Form + closest Technique + Aura + stress dice (modified by Virtues and Flaws)

title: Transitory Magic Items
heading: Transitory Magic Items
summary: Introduces single-use items made by Faerie-aligned Egyptian magicians that are not enchanted but carry a supernatural property, commonly temporary amulets and potions.
quotes: A transitory magic item is an object which has supernatural properties, but only for a single use

title: Temporary Amulets (Until Duration)
heading: Temporary Amulets
summary: A temporary amulet is an object carrying a spell with the Faerie-only Until Duration that ends when the amulet is worn and discarded, and the effect survives its creator's death.
quotes: an object on which a spell with the Until Duration has been cast

title: The Statues Just Hold Faeries, They Are Not Enchanted
heading: The Statues Just Hold Faeries, They Are Not Enchanted
summary: Merinita view that holy statues, such as a cippus of Horus, are open offers to faeries who feed on the worshipers' hope, rather than enchanted items.
quotes: it's a clever way of making an open offer to nearby faeries

title: Egyptian Seals (temporary magic items)
heading: Seals
summary: Seals hold a spell maintained by an Until Duration or act like Watching Wards, triggering when a precondition (usually breaking the seal) is met.
quotes: Egyptian seals of this type are remarkably similar to Watching Wards.

title: Temporary Potions
heading: Temporary Potions
summary: Potions made by pouring water or beer over a statue housing a faerie (such as a cippus of Horus) or over inscribed bowls, each giving a single effect if a nearby faerie accepts the deal.
quotes: Each statue provided a single effect.

title: The Drawing of Maat (tongue magic)
heading: The Drawing of Maat
summary: A lost technique of painting the goddess of Truth on the tongue that prevents lying and, once its Mystery is found, creates a tiny possessing faerie that corrects mispronunciation so botches are less likely.
quotes: The faerie checks his words for mispronunciations and corrects them

title: Saliva and Breath Ranges
heading: Saliva and Breath Ranges
summary: Spitting or breathing on a target counts as a Range equivalent to Personal, but without bypassing Magic Resistance as Personal spells do, making some Spontaneous spells easier.
quotes: Treat this as equivalent to Personal range, but without circumventing Magic resistance as Personal spells do.

title: Statue Consecration
heading: Statue Consecration Mystery
summary: How chief lectors consecrate a new statue so a faerie inhabits it, by performing a ritual narrative that faeries feed on; the roll is aided by a Faerie aura. Sidebars give examples of animated models and the play of faeries against one another.
quotes: This requires a Communication + Folk Ken roll against a target of 18.

title: Unusual Amulets: Ib Scarab and Royal Names
heading: Unusual Amulets
summary: The Ib Scarab replaces the heart and works at Personal Range, and seals with royal names carry a little Magic Resistance that may accidentally protect a wearer from curses.
quotes: it replaces the heart, and so can create effects at Personal Range.
These royal names have a little Magic Resistance, perhaps as high as 5 points.

title: Temporary Objects From Models
heading: Temporary Objects From Models
summary: Model objects in tombs can become temporary real objects with a faerie inside; troupes without Realms of Power: Faerie design it as a shapeshifting magic item.
quotes: Groups using only the core rules should design a magic item with a shapeshifting effect.

title: Threatening the Gods
heading: Threatening the Gods
summary: Describes the alternative Enchantment Faerie Rite Method in which a caster threatens to destroy a faerie and the world unless given what is demanded, and who used it.
quotes: The spell-caster threatened to destroy not only the faerie, but the entire world, unless given what was demanded.

title: The Weakest and Commonest Ancient Magicians
heading: The Weakest and Commonest Ancient Magicians
summary: Describes local-spirit priests like village witches and suggests ways to design them, such as Faerie Friend, Faerie Doctors or Faerie Bargainers, with their grave goods as Mystery quest goals.
quotes: Some of these priests of local gods could be designed as Faerie Doctors

title: Writings of Those Who Threatened the Gods
heading: The Writings of Those Who Threatened the Gods
summary: Three kinds of recoverable texts: Enchant-scripts, threat scripts that add a bonus to a Rite's casting total, and Mystery initiation texts granting Virtues such as Puissant Enchantment.
quotes: These grant a bonus to the casting total of a particular Rite.

title: Magical Craftwork
heading: Magical Craftwork
summary: Introduces the caste of magical crafters who made amulets, talismans and curses, whose writings produced the Learned Magician tradition and remain usable by Coptic speakers.

title: Egyptian Craft Magic and Learned Magic
heading: Relationship to Learned Magic
requires: Learned Magician rules (Hedge Magic: Revised Edition)
summary: Shows how to simulate Ancient Egyptian amulets, talismans and curses with Learned Magic Techniques and Forms, noting that Egyptian magic lacks the Range, Target and Duration limits and Difficult Arts, and assumes high casting and lab totals.
quotes: Troupes using the Learned Magician rules to create Egyptian spells should assume that the Egyptians had very high casting and laboratory totals

title: Contained Spirits
heading: Contained Spirits
summary: Rules of thumb for creatures trapped in containers: bargains bind only the words spoken, a spirit can be won as a permanent ally by favors comparable to Mystery Ordeals, and freeing a faerie unconditionally invites a gift in return.
quotes: A bargain struck with these beings is binding, but only the specific words, not the intent, need to be adhered to.
A rescued spirit may be converted into a permanent ally by performing a series of favors for it.

title: A Note on True Names
heading: A Note on True Names
summary: Explains Egyptian casualness about True Names (ka names, rens) listed in tombs and how shabti servants answer the name and shift the target of curses.
quotes: The owner had shabtis, little statue servants, who answered his True Name for him.

title: The Book of Thoth
heading: Those Who Have Read the Book of Thoth
summary: A character who reads the Book of Thoth can effortlessly cast almost any Hermetic spell but dies or fades into Twilight within a day, after which the Book is hidden again.
quotes: Within one day, however, they either die or fade into Twilight.

title: Auras in Egypt
heading: A Note on Auras in Egypt
summary: Gives typical Dominion aura strengths for holy sites, graves, workplaces and the call to prayer, how to set Faerie auras from the strongest faerie's Might, where Magic auras come from, and Infernal auras.
quotes: Faerie auras are equal to (Might of the most powerful faerie in the area /5)

generally places of worship have a Dominion aura of 4, the cemeteries and homes of the People of the Book have an aura of 3, the places of work of monotheists have an aura of 2, and land from which the call to prayer can be heard has an aura of 1
